why: Rule 1 / hot-blob trap: the 247k e/cm 2.4 cm proton stub leaves 11000 at a large angle from the flat 70-80k MIP pion, so this is a two-prong junction, not the Bragg peak of one track.

Rule 8 event - only seven sub-cm blobs with no measured dQ/dx and no direction anywhere; picked the blob at the centroid of the compact five-blob group near (-110,-113,286), which is separated from the two far blobs at y=+130. Essentially a guess among five.
Rule 1 on a lone 11 cm proton: dQ/dx falls monotonically along the proton template from 211k at 13000 to 50k at 13002, so the track starts at 13002.
Rule 1: two proton segments (37.9 cm and 4.9 cm) both show monotone Bragg rises away from 20002 to their far ends, leaving 20002 at about 90 degrees.

Rules 6/7 on a fragmented two-arm EM event with no track; picked the degree-3 apex of the largest shower cluster where a short 2.2-MIP stub attaches, but both arms look like photon conversions so the true vertex may be invisible.
Rule 1 at a degree-4 junction: the 28.6 cm segment rises away from 5002 to its hot stop at 5004, the other three prongs are flat, and the shower fragments trail downstream from 5002.
Rule 1 with two Bragg ends: the 18.3 cm and 7.7 cm proton segments each rise monotonically along the proton template to their far ends and meet at 14002 in a 44-degree V.
Rule 1 plus the hot-blob trap: the 7 cm proton Braggs away to 18002 while the 102 cm muon is flat MIP for 100 cm with only a two-point spike at 18001, i.e. vertex charge and not a Bragg rise.

Rule 1: the 10 cm pi+ has a clean Bragg rise to 118k at 7005, so the vertex is the cool end of the chain; 7002 is the degree-2 kink (118 degrees) with locally elevated charge, 2.6 cm inside the free tip 7000.
Rule 8 abstention: four isolated blobs of 3.5 cm or less, spread 30-70 cm apart with no readable direction and no ionizing structure, so any click is as good as another.
The only ionizing object in the event is a 2.4 cm 240k e/cm proton; the vertex is at one of its ends and rule 2 (beam-forward, lower z) picks 16001, but the end choice is close to a coin flip.
Rule 1: the 8.6 cm proton Braggs away to 230k at 8003 and the 71 cm flat-MIP muon leaves at 68 degrees, with the charge concentration sitting exactly at 8040.

Rules 1 and 3: the 24 cm muon rises to 101k and stops at 11000 with a Michel-like blob 4.3 cm off that end, so the vertex is the cool upstream tip 11001. The competing 11002 is a 146-degree degree-2 junction (trap 3) where both segments read ~1 MIP with no junction charge, so I read its 34-degree non-MCS kink as a hard scatter of one particle rather than a vertex.
Rule 1 in its cleanest form: a degree-3 vertex with all three attached segments (proton, muon, shower) rising away from it, 3 of 3.

Rule 1 at the degree-3 hub carrying the 24 cm proton that Braggs away to 265k at 7005 and the 55 cm MIP muon; it is also the lowest-z candidate, though the second hub 7009 12 cm away has its own proton.
